title: DeepResearch Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Deep Research Agents
publisher: arXiv (Mingxuan Du, Benfeng Xu, Chiwei Zhu, Xiaorui Wang, Zhendong Mao)

key_points.claim: Deep Research Agents (DRAs) are defined as LLM agents that do multistep web exploration, targeted retrieval and synthesis to produce citation-rich reports.
key_points.evidence_quote: By autonomously orchestrating multistep web exploration, targeted retrieval, and higher-order synthesis, they transform vast amounts of online information into analyst-grade, citation-rich reports

key_points.claim: The authors say that before this work there was no comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating DRAs.
key_points.evidence_quote: a comprehensive benchmark for systematically evaluating the capabilities of these agents remains absent

key_points.claim: DeepResearch Bench contains 100 PhD-level research tasks written by domain experts across 22 fields.
key_points.evidence_quote: a benchmark consisting of 100 PhD-level research tasks, each meticulously crafted by domain experts across 22 distinct fields

key_points.claim: Evaluating DRAs is described as complex and labor-intensive, so the authors propose automated methods that they say align well with human judgment.
key_points.evidence_quote: Evaluating DRAs is inherently complex and labor-intensive. We therefore propose two novel methodologies that achieve strong alignment with human judgment.

key_points.claim: Report quality is scored with a reference-based method that uses adaptive criteria (later known as RACE).
key_points.evidence_quote: The first is a reference-based method with adaptive criteria to assess the quality of generated research reports.

key_points.claim: A second framework (later known as FACT) scores retrieval and information-collection ability using effective citation count and citation accuracy.
key_points.evidence_quote: evaluate DRA's information retrieval and collection capabilities by assessing its effective citation count and overall citation accuracy

key_points.claim: The benchmark and key parts of the evaluation frameworks are open-sourced.
key_points.evidence_quote: We have open-sourced DeepResearch Bench and key components of these frameworks at https://github.com/Ayanami0730/deep_research_bench

reliability_notes: Only the arXiv abstract page was retrieved; the 31-page full paper was not read. That means there are no specific results, model rankings, or human-agreement figures here. The page gives no names for the two methods; RACE and FACT are the names used in the paper itself, supplied from background knowledge rather than this source. This is a preprint (v1, June 2025) and not peer-reviewed. The claim of 'strong alignment with human judgment' is the authors' own and is not quantified on this page.
